newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet backs 100 bln baht zero-coupon bond.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet backs 100 bln baht zero-coupon bond.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved a proposal by the finance ministry and Bank of Thailand for the government to float up to 100 billion baht ($3.87 billion), seven-year zero-coupon bonds, a government spokesman said.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said earlier proceeds from the bond issue would be used for refinancing troubled property projects and for easing liquidity problems of their creditors in bank and finance company sectors.

The central bank said in a separate statement that funds raised by the bonds would be loaned to property projects under development at market interest rates so that their indebted developers could pay off unserviced borrowing owed to financial institutions.
It said financial institutions whose doubtful property loans were trimmed by government assistance would have to guarantee a 50 percent repayment of the refinanced loans extended by the government.
Governor Rerngchai said on Tuesday that the 50 percent repayment guarantee would be regarded as contingent liability of financial institutions.
He said the new loans would be managed by a new government body called Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO).

The governor said: "The property loan refinancing would help trim non-performing loan portfolios of financial institutions. Together with higher provisions for sub-standard assets required by the government last week, financial statements (of these institutions) for the next accounting period would look better."
